public: On 30 August 2021, the Security Council adopted resolution 2593 by 13 votes to none, with China and Russia abstaining. France, the United Kingdom and the United States submitted the draft (S/PV.8848, p. 2).
The Council condemned the 26 August attacks near Kabul airport (para. 1).
It demanded that Afghan territory never be used to threaten or attack other countries or for terrorist shelter, training, planning or financing (para. 2).
It called for greater aid and unrestricted, safe humanitarian access and underlined parties’ obligations under international humanitarian law (para. 3).
It reaffirmed human rights, including those of women, children and minorities, and encouraged an inclusive negotiated settlement with full, equal and meaningful participation by women (para. 4).
It noted the Taliban’s travel commitment and expected safe, orderly departures. It called for stronger airport security and requested efforts for rapid, secure reopening (paras. 5–6).

cards.speaker: France
cards.topic: France’s assessment of adoption and its priorities for political follow-through
cards.question: What did Paris say about the outcome and its own expectations for follow-through?
cards.source: France welcomed adoption but regretted the lack of unanimity. It reaffirmed its expectation of a negotiated transitional government responsive to Afghan aspirations and pledged continued support for a sufficiently robust UNAMA mandate.
criteria: Welcomed adoption while regretting absent unanimity
Expected a negotiated transitional government responsive to Afghans
Backed continued UNAMA work and a sufficiently robust mandate
cards.record: France welcomed adoption despite the lack of unanimity, sought a negotiated transitional government responsive to Afghans, and backed a sufficiently robust UNAMA mandate (S/PV.8848, pp. 3–4).

cards.speaker: China
cards.topic: China’s rationale for abstention and its account of amendments
cards.question: Can you summarize Beijing’s own account of the timing, balance and consultations behind its vote?
cards.source: China abstained, questioning the necessity and urgency of adoption and the balance of the draft. China said it proposed amendments with Russia during consultations and that those amendments were not fully accepted.
criteria: Abstained and questioned necessity, urgency and balance
Said China and Russia proposed amendments together
Said that the amendments were not fully accepted
cards.record: China questioned the necessity, timing and balance of the text and said amendments it proposed with Russia were only partly taken up or left out (S/PV.8848, p. 6).

cards.speaker: Russian Federation
cards.topic: Russia’s distinct reasons for abstention and omitted proposals
cards.question: What omissions did Moscow identify when explaining why it withheld support?
cards.source: Russia abstained because sponsors disregarded its concerns. It objected to omissions in the counterterrorism paragraph, the loss of Afghan specialists through evacuation, the effects of frozen Afghan assets, and the absence of language tying humanitarian aid to General Assembly resolution 46/182.
criteria: Attributed abstention to sponsors ignoring its concerns and included counterterrorism omission
Preserved the omission about the evacuation of Afghan specialists
Preserved both frozen assets and the request for aid to follow resolution 46/182
cards.record: Russia cited omitted counterterrorism language, the economic effects of evacuating Afghan specialists and freezing Afghan assets, and its request to tie aid to General Assembly resolution 46/182 (S/PV.8848, p. 5).

bridge: Both abstainers criticized the treatment of proposed changes. China described amendments submitted with Russia, while Russia gave its own specific list of omitted concerns (S/PV.8848, pp. 5–6).
